messages:
marta: Hi team — customer on Private (VPC) reporting intermittent TLS handshake failures when calling Redwood API through their corporate proxy. Error from client: "SSL: certificate verify failed / no shared cipher". Ticket #INC-4127.

marta: Repro steps they gave:
1) From their app host inside VPC -> curl https://api.redwood.example.com/generate -v
2) Request fails immediately with TLS alert.
3) If they bypass proxy, call succeeds.

devops_jay: Can you paste the curl -v / openssl output? Also which proxy appliance/version?

marta: They supplied the curl debug:

```
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood.example.com/generate/
*   Trying 10.20.30.40...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood.example.com (10.20.30.40) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* SSL connection using TLSv1.2 / ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384
* error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:unknown protocol
* SSL: no shared cipher
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) SSL: no shared cipher
```

ana: small correction: that curl line is odd — it claims TLSv1.2 + ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384 but then unknown protocol. Could be the middlebox rewriting or terminating TLS and re-initiating with a different profile. What does openssl s_client show if they connect via proxy (CONNECT)?

marta: They ran openssl against the proxied route (via CONNECT) and captured this: 

```
$ openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example.com:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com -proxy 10.1.1.1:3128
CONNECTED(00000005)
140735123456000:error:1417A0C1:SSL routines:tls_process_server_certificate:certificate verify failed:ssl/t1_lib.c:?
---
Server certificate
subject=/CN=api.redwood.example.com
issuer=/CN=corp-intermediate
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIB... (truncated)
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
---
No client certificate CA names sent
---
SSL handshake has read 1987 bytes and written 512 bytes
---
New, TLSv1/SSLv3, Cipher is (NONE)
*** TLS handshake failure
```

ana: Looks like the proxy is intercepting and presenting its own cert (corp-intermediate). Two possibilities: (1) proxy is performing TLS MITM and refuses ECDSA-signed upstream certs / or strips TLS1.3 ciphers, or (2) proxy only supports RSA-based handshakes with certain cipher suites. Customer said their gateway is Palo Alto with SSL Forward Proxy enabled and a strict cipher profile.

ryan-support: Quick checklist for customer: 
- Confirm proxy cipher/profile allows ECDHE+ECDSA or enable ECDSA algorithms.
- If their proxy terminates TLS, ensure it trusts Redwood's CA chain and does not downgrade to a cipher the client/server don't share.
- Temporarily test by allowing TLS1.3 and modern ciphers or by disabling SSL Forward Proxy for the Redwood host as a test.

marta: They tried changing the proxy profile to "Modern" per vendor docs but still sees handshake fail. They captured proxy logs showing "ssl-decrypt: no compatible signature algorithm".

ana: That string suggests the proxy is negotiating based on signature algorithms and possibly rejecting ECDSA-signed certs upstream. What is Redwood Private's cert sig alg? We typically offer ECDSA leaf certs. If the middlebox lacks ECDSA support it will fail to validate/forward.

devops_jay: Two mitigations we can recommend: 
1) Customer: Allow ECDSA signature algs / update middlebox firmware to support modern curves.
2) Customer: Configure proxy to pass-through TLS for the Redwood host (no TLS interception).
3) Redwood-side workaround: offer an RSA-signed certificate for their private deployment (they can upload an alternate cert) or enable an RSA keypair for the endpoint.

marta: Customer says they can't disable SSL Forward Proxy for compliance. They're open to uploading an RSA cert. How do they do that for Private?

ryan-support: Guide them: In the Private console -> Networking -> TLS certs -> Upload custom cert + private key (PEM). Note: key must be RSA if proxy requires RSA. I'll paste snippet: 

```
# Example curl to test forcing RSA TLS handshake
curl --tlsv1.2 --ciphers 'ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384' https://api.redwood.example.com/generate -v
```

ana: Also request they run a cipher-scan from inside their VPC to the proxied endpoint: `nmap --script ssl-enum-ciphers -p 443 <proxy-ip>` or use `testssl.sh` to see supported sigalgs. That will show whether proxy accepts ECDSA.

marta: Customer ran testssl and proxy reports supported sigalgs: `RSA+SHA256, RSA+SHA1`. No ECDSA entries. So middlebox only supports RSA-signed cert chains.

devops_jay: Ok that explains it. We should escalate a documentation note: for Private/VPC deployments behind intercepting proxies that only accept RSA, customers must either upload an RSA cert or enable pass-through. I'll create an internal doc PR.

ingress-monitor-bot: Incident INC-4127 created and assigned to #support; priority P2.

ryan-support: Final customer guidance sent: (1) upload RSA cert to Private, (2) test with `curl --tlsv1.2 --ciphers 'ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384'`, (3) if impossible, request proxy vendor firmware update to add ECDSA/sigalg support.

marta: I'll close the slack loop once they confirm RSA cert upload works. Thanks all :thumbsup:

ryan-support: marking for follow-up with eng-runtime so we can add a KB about cert signature compatibility in Private docs.
